cards.explanation: The answer is False. The text says Jehoahaz "…did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as his fathers had done." He was twenty-three when he became king, and he reigned three months. A short reign, friends, and the verdict is already written.

The answer is: so he can't reign in Jerusalem. The text gives the reason plainly. Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt, imprisoned Jehoahaz at Riblah "…so that he could not reign in Jerusalem…" Nobody has to guess, friends, because the verse hands it right over.

The answer is Pharaoh Neco. The text says Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt, "…made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of his father Josiah…" The one who made him king was Egypt's king. That's the whole answer the verse gives, friends.

The answer is that Neco carries him off to Egypt. The text says Neco "…took Jehoahaz and carried him off to Egypt…" Pharaoh Neco was Egypt's king. So Jehoahaz went from prison at Riblah to Egypt, friends.
The answer is True. The text says Neco carried Jehoahaz off to Egypt, "…where he died." He was twenty-three when he became king. It's a sad ending, friends, and the text states it plainly.

The answer is wealth. Jehoiakim taxed the land and took the silver and gold from the people, "…each according to his wealth." So the amount depended on what each person had. Pharaoh Neco sent the bill, and the people of Judah got handed the payment, friends.

The answer is that he serves Nebuchadnezzar. The text says Jehoiakim "…became his vassal for three years…" A vassal is a king who answers to a stronger king. So the man Pharaoh Neco put on the throne now answers to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. New boss, same throne, so somebody update the org chart, friends.

The answer is True. The text says Jehoiakim served for three years "…until he turned and rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar." Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon. So Jehoiakim went from serving him to turning against him, friends.

The answer is the LORD. The text says, "…the LORD sent Chaldean, Aramean, Moabite, and Ammonite raiders against Jehoiakim in order to destroy Judah…" It happened "…according to the word that the LORD had spoken through His servants the prophets." These raiders came because the LORD sent them, friends.

The answer is False. The text says Manasseh "…had filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the LORD was unwilling to forgive." Manasseh was an earlier king of Judah (2 Kings 21:1). This is a heavy part of the story, friends, and the text says it straight.

The answer is his son Jehoiachin. The text says Jehoiakim "…rested with his fathers, and his son Jehoiachin reigned in his place." The throne went from father to son. That's a different pattern from the first half of the passage, friends, where Pharaoh Neco did the choosing.

The answer is that Babylon had taken all his territory. The king of Egypt did not march out of his land again "…because the king of Babylon had taken all his territory, from the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates River." That's a big stretch of land, friends. The king of Babylon's reach was now much bigger.
